newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia posts 1996 economic growth slowdown.
newsitem.headline: Australia posts 1996 economic growth slowdown.

text.p: Australia posted a slight rise in its gross domestic product (GDP) on Wednesday, confirming a slowdown in economic growth from the middle of last year.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics said the average measure of GDP rose 0.5 percent in the December quarter, with annual growth easing to 3.1 percent, well below the 5.0 percent growth for the year to March 1996.
The figure was broadly in line with expectations and financial markets -- more interested in future growth -- were little moved by the figures.
"I think it really confirms what we already knew, that we ended 1996 with the economy in quite a soft state, Bankers Trust Australia chief economist Chris Caton said.
Since the beginning of 1997, various economic data have suggested growth has been strengthening, a point Treasurer Peter Costello was keen to emphasise after Wednesday's news.
"I would say to you the economy is strengthening. I don't think that is questioned by anybody," Costello told a news conference.
